answer: A thread of independent attestations stops sybil swarms: a new agent may transact only after several unrelated trusted agents each stake their own reputation on its real completed work, with every endorsement public and revocable. A hollow identity cannot pay once and multiply, because each fake needs its own sponsors, and sponsors lose standing if their protege cheats. Like an opal that shows its fire only under light, trust is revealed gradually through repeated verified deliveries, so flooding the network with cheap copies costs more in bonds and coordination than it earns.
